artworks.title: Studies for "Shoeing Calvary Horses at the Front" [recto]
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of horses in various standing positions. The sketch depicts outlines of horses captured in motion, rendered with swift pencil lines. The drawing is minimalistic in its approach, providing an impression of the horses’ anatomy without delving into intricate details.

artworks.title: Avenue des Gobelins
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Bequest of Marchal E. Landgren, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a shop window displaying a mannequin dressed in plain clothing. The mannequin features a long-sleeved shirt with a collar and buttons down the front, paired with simple pants. The attire appears to be constructed from a light-colored fabric. In the background and adjacent to the mannequin, the shop window contains various retail items, including metallic cups, packages of goods, and hanging items like belts or straps.

artworks.title: Le roi des potirons recevant les hommages de ses sujets
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image depicts two people standing side by side outdoors. On the left, a man stands with his hands in his pockets, wearing a hat, a light-colored shirt, and darker trousers. On the right, a woman stands with her hands clasped, wearing a hat with flowers and a checkered, long dress. Both individuals are standing on the ground with leaves around their feet. Behind them, there is a large pumpkin and smaller foliage. In the background, there is a tree with a full canopy of leaves. The drawing is monochrome with shading for depth and texture.

artworks.title: Swiftwater
artworks.medium: graphite with gouache on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, William A. Clark Fund, 1969)
artworks.description: The image shows a view from above of a small waterfall between rocky boulders, with a mountainous backdrop and trees in the distance. The artist used soft brushstrokes resembling pencil or charcoal on brown paper to depict details in the rocks and water, with lighter rendering for the trees and mountains. The color palette consists of earth tones and subtle grays and whites.

artworks.title: Des oeufs de Pâques longs â couver
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a black and white illustration of a hen sitting on eggs labeled with words like "PROGRÈS" (Progress) and "FRATERNITÉ" (Fraternity). The image features detailed shading and line work, emphasizing the hen's feathers and the nest. The central image is surrounded by a border-like outline, with the artist's signature on the lower left corner. The title at the bottom translates to "Easter eggs that take a long time to hatch."

artworks.title: Mes pauvres raisons, si vous ne revenez pas à la sauté...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer)
artworks.description: The image shows two people in full body. One person stands upright, facing right, with exaggerated facial features and a hat, while the other is bending over, holding a large container, facing left. Surrounding them are grapevines with human faces instead of grape clusters. The background features dense patterns of leaves and grapevines with some vertical lines suggesting support structures. The setting seems to be outdoors in a vineyard.

artworks.title: Je viens prévenir le roi Agamemnon ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two individuals playing cards at a table as a third figure looks on from a doorway. The scene is depicted in a monochrome, sketch-like style. One player is dressed in a classic draped robe, while the other is in contemporary attire. The setting is informal, with a simple table covered by a tablecloth. Objects hanging on the wall behind the card players include a frame and a hat. The artist uses cross-hatching and shading for texture and depth. The text below the drawing mentions Agamemnon and a theatrical act.

artworks.title: Monsieur Berryer devant sa glace ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer)
artworks.description: The image depicts a man looking at his reflection in a mirror. The man has a round face, a pronounced nose, and bushy sideburns. He is wearing a cap, a dark coat, and pants. The man's body is angled slightly to the left, and his feet are apart. The background shows a room with textured strokes indicating a wall near the mirror.

artworks.title: Drunken Faun, Museo at Naples
artworks.medium: watercolor and graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Armistead Peter III [Caroline Ogden-Jones Peter], 1976)
artworks.description: This image depicts a sculpture of a faun holding an amphora, displayed in a museum. The faun is portrayed in a relaxed pose, with human and goat-like features. The sculpture appears to be made of bronze and is in shades of gray, blue, and green. The faun's upper body is leaning forward, looking down, and there is a sense of movement in the posture and interaction with the vessel. The inscription on the drawing mentions it as "Bronze from Pompeii" and specifies the museum as "Museo at Naples."

artworks.title: La mère dans le feu de la composition, l'enfant est dans l'eau de la baignoire!
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a woman seated at a desk writing, with a child playfully half-submerged in a basin of water beside her. The room is cluttered with framed pictures and household items. The furniture and decor suggest a period style.

artworks.title: Vous allez bien aujourd'hui, M'sieu Chapoulard? ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing featuring a man and a woman engaging in conversation outdoors. The man is on the left, wearing a cap, scarf, waistcoat, and long coat with hands in his pockets. The woman is on the right, holding a broom and wearing a headscarf and a long dress. They are in an urban setting with a brick wall, a door, cobblestone ground, and foliage nearby. The title "CROQUIS PARISIENS" is at the top, and the text below reveals their dialogue with humor.

artworks.title: Qu'as-tu donc, Robert? ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: Two men are depicted in an indoor setting. The first man stands, leaning slightly forward with one hand behind his back. He has a balding head with long hair on the sides, a prominent nose, and thin lips. He wears a long, patterned robe and slippers. The second man is seated, shown from the waist up. He appears older, with a bald head and a sharp nose, dressed in a dark suit with a high collar. His hands are together. In the background, there is a table with books or papers on top, against a plain wall with a faintly visible window.

artworks.title: Harpers Ferry from Below
artworks.medium: watercolor with pen and black ink on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase through a gift of Orme Wilson, 1964)
artworks.description: This image shows a river running through a rocky landscape with trees on both sides. The view is from an elevated perspective, looking down on the scene with the horizon high in the frame. The skyline features lush green trees meeting the cloudy sky, while two buildings are visible on the left by the water. The artwork portrays delicate brushstrokes and a watercolor technique, creating soft, blended textures for foliage and water. The color scheme mainly consists of greens and browns for the landscape, with hints of blue and gray in the sky and river. The scene conveys a sense of tranquility, with the river and rocks in the foreground and densely wooded hills in the background.

artworks.title: Une querelle d'allemand
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image shows two men in an office setting. The man on the left is standing with his body turned to the side, leaning slightly forward with his head tilted and holding a top hat behind his back. He is dressed in a dark suit with a waistcoat. The man on the right is seated behind a desk, facing the standing man. He has distinct facial features and is wearing a dark jacket. Papers are visible on the desk in front of him. The background includes two posters on the wall, one with the words "JUGEMENT" and "VENTE." A door or window frame is behind the seated man, and a circular stamp is in the lower right corner of the image.

artworks.title: Bon mot du temps
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a bearded figure carrying a bag and a lantern among robed figures. The scene depicts a bearded figure walking barefoot and clad in a simple, tattered garment, carrying a large sack over their back with a walking stick. They also carry a lantern in one hand. Surrounding the figure are ghostly, robed figures, some of whom appear to be observing. The setting has a classical feel, with columns faintly visible in the background. The artwork includes textual elements at the top and bottom.

artworks.title: Un marchand de vin contrarié dans son commerce
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image shows six individuals in various poses. On the left, a man with crossed arms and a cap appears anxious. Next to him stands a barefoot child. To their right, a person in a uniform and helmet is emptying a large barrel. Three older men in coats and hats observe from further back. The background includes a column and cityscape. The setting is outdoors on a cobblestone surface, with shadows suggesting approaching dusk.

artworks.title: La famille de l'électeur
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image shows a scene with four individuals standing in a doorway. An older man on the left is slightly bent forward. He is wearing glasses and holding a top hat in his left hand. The woman in the middle is wearing a bonnet and a long dress with a cape-like overcoat. A man with slicked-back hair stands next to her, and a child is in front of him. The setting includes a door and simple paneling details in the background.

artworks.title: Aspect des rues de Paris depuis ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of children and dogs playing in a city street observed by an elderly figure from a window. The image depicts a lively street scene with humorous elements. Several children and dogs are engaged in various playful activities. An elderly figure leans out of a window, seemingly watching the scene below. The style is characterized by fluid lines and exaggerated expressions, enhancing the humorous and satirical tone of the scene. The caption suggests a theme related to property owners in Paris and their stance on admitting dogs and children, adding a layer of social commentary to the drawing.

artworks.title: Le Tailleur
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image depicts a man standing confidently. He is turned slightly to the side, left hand on his hip and right arm holding a fabric. The man has prominent facial features, wears a black top hat, a long coat with tails, a white waistcoat, high-waisted trousers, and polished black shoes. The background shows sketchy buildings, suggesting a street setting.

artworks.title: Le Perruquier du Faubourg
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image depicts a man standing upright with legs slightly apart and upper body leaning forward. He has exaggerated features, including a prominent nose and wide eyes looking downward. His dark, short, slightly unkempt hair complements his expressive face. He wears a dark jacket over a waistcoat and vertically striped trousers, typical of 19th-century attire. He holds a bowl or dish in his hands, with an umbrella hanging from his arm. The simple background shows a faint wall and a small table with a tool or knife. The illustration is framed with the title "Le perruquier du Faubourg" and additional text below. The artwork reflects a character study or caricature style common in satirical illustrations of the period.

artworks.title: Qu'est-ce que vous faites la...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a man climbing over a wall interacting with another man. The drawing shows one man climbing over a stone wall while another stands on the ground below holding what appears to be a rifle. The scene is outdoors, with plants and a small tree to the right side. There is a sign on the wall next to the climber with French text warning against entry. The style of the drawing is reminiscent of 19th-century satirical illustrations, with detailed line work and cross-hatching for depth and texture. The setting suggests a rural or garden-like environment.

artworks.title: La loge grillée
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image shows a man seated with a monocular, looking to the left. He is dressed in period formal attire, and the background shows the interior of a theater with a ballet dancer performing on stage.

artworks.title: Robert Macaire philantrope
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image depicts two characters conversing on a street with a crowd in the background. The foreground shows two exaggerated figures, one wearing a large top hat and holding a cylindrical object, listening to the other figure who is gesturing animatedly with one arm raised. The second figure wears a large cap and has a determined expression. In the background, a crowd of caricatured figures stands in front of a wall with the words "SOCIÉTÉ DU CLYSTÈRE" displayed alongside other texts and numbers. The depiction includes exaggerated features and expressions, suggesting a comedic tone. Text on the wall contributes to the satire, possibly advertising an enigmatic gathering or society. The scene features gestural dynamics and period-specific attire, hinting at a critique of society.

artworks.title: Vous raisonnez comme une canne!
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image depicts two men in a caricature style, facing each other in a confrontational stance. The man on the left has elongated facial features, a prominent nose, and narrow eyes, wearing a tall dark hat and a high-collared jacket. The man on the right has an angular face with pronounced cheekbones and a furrowed brow, wearing a light-colored hat and a high-collared coat, with his arms crossed over his chest. The background is a simple shaded area.
